archetype.name: Retooling (offense-carried, secondary leaking)
archetype.definition: A team built around Jayden Daniels that can score with anyone when he plays, but whose pass defense and special teams give back more than the offense makes, leaving the 2024 breakout looking more like the exception than the baseline.

report.headline: Daniels keeps them competitive; a leaky secondary and bad special teams keep them losing.
report.take:
Washington is 1-3-1 and getting outscored by 6.8 points a game, and the record is close to honest: wins over expected sits at -0.34, so this isn't a good team running into bad luck. The profile is a league-average offense (16th in EPA, 23 points a game) attached to a defense that ranks 24th in EPA allowed and 30th in points allowed. The pieces don't net out. Special teams make it worse, costing nearly three points of EPA a game, 28th in the league.

The defense is two different units. Against the run it is genuinely good: 7th in rush EPA allowed and 3rd in explosive run rate allowed. Offenses have figured that out and throw on it at a rate 6.1 points above normal, the 3rd-strongest pass funnel in the league. Through the air it is 25th in EPA allowed. Seattle threw for 393 yards on it, the Giants for 326, and tight ends have feasted, with the opponent's TE1 scoring 10.7 PPR points over his average, worst in the league. The pressure rate is middling, but it rarely finishes: the sack rate is 27th. In the red zone, opponents have scored touchdowns on 83% of trips, dead last. The bend-don't-break idea isn't holding.

What the numbers hide is how much is propping this up. Washington is +1 in turnovers per game, 4th in the league, with seven takeaways against two giveaways, and it still has one win. That is the stat that usually flatters a record, and it is the most likely to regress. The offense also splits cleanly by quarterback: 25.5 points a game in Daniels' four starts, 13 in Mariota's one. The run game piles up yards in good scripts (182 at Dallas, 202 against the Giants), but overall rush EPA is 21st and success rate 27th. It gains volume more than efficiency.

The history matters here. This is the third straight year of a bottom-ten defense, and the 2025 unit was 31st, so a 24th-place ranking counts as improvement. The 12-win 2024 season came with +2.78 wins over expected, and 2025 swung back to 5 wins. This roster looks like the middle of that range, not the top of it.

strengths.title: Run defense that shuts the door
strengths.body: Washington allows -0.177 EPA per rush and almost no explosive runs, which is why opponents abandon the ground against it. It is a real, repeatable strength that showed up again against Seattle, who managed 44 rushing yards. The catch is that it pushes the pressure onto the weakest part of the defense.

strengths.title: Daniels-led offense moves the ball
strengths.body: With Daniels under center, the offense has scored 20 or more in all four starts. The line gets backs 2.88 yards before contact (7th) and keeps the sack rate at 5.1% (9th), though the Giants' five sacks are a warning. Passing EPA is positive at 0.073, mid-pack but workable.

strengths.title: Winning the turnover battle
strengths.body: A +1 turnover margin per game has kept two of these games close. It's genuine in the sense that Daniels hasn't been careless, but takeaway runs this hot rarely last, so don't count on it as a pillar.

concerns.title: Pass defense is a funnel to failure
concerns.body: Opponents throw more than they should against Washington because it works: 25th in pass EPA allowed, 27th in success rate allowed, and the league's worst red-zone touchdown rate. Part of this is structural, since a strong run defense invites passes. But the pass rush doesn't finish, and the safety room is now gutted, with Nick Cross (99% of snaps), Percy Butler and Tyler Owens all out and Trey Amos on IR. It gets worse before it gets better.

concerns.title: Special teams bleeding points
concerns.body: At -2.92 EPA per game, the third phase costs roughly a field goal every week. Over five games that is about the gap between 1-3-1 and .500. There is no sign in the data that it is a fluke.

concerns.title: Inefficient run game dressed in yards
concerns.body: The run game has two 180-plus yard days, but overall rush EPA is -0.144 and success rate is 27th. The yards come when the script is friendly, not as a way to control games. Against a strong front, that volume tends to disappear.

trend.note: Results have been tied to the quarterback and to takeaways: competitive in every Daniels start (covering at Philly, outlasting Seattle 33-31, tying the Giants) and a 17-point loss in Mariota's one start. The defense has allowed 300-plus passing yards in two of the last three games.

nextGame.headline: The league's best passing offense meets a secondary missing three safeties
nextGame.body:
San Francisco is the worst possible opponent for this defense. The 49ers lead the league in pass EPA (0.389) and success rate, and their line allows pressure on just 10.2% of dropbacks, best in football. Washington already struggles to finish rushes, and Purdy should get clean pockets against a secondary that leaks. On the other side, Washington's run-first lean runs straight into a defense that is 4th against the run and 1st in explosive plays allowed both ways. Opponents keep running on the 49ers (a -5.6 pass rate over norm) and keep failing.

Availability cuts both ways, but more against Washington. The Commanders are without Stefon Diggs, their target leader, plus Cross, Butler, Owens, Omenihu and Amos. The 49ers lose Deebo Samuel and Christian Kirk at receiver and Marques Sigle at safety, Dre Greenlaw is suspended, and Nick Bosa is only a 'chance' to play. If Bosa sits, Daniels' pocket gets easier after he took five sacks last week. That is the main thing that could keep this close.

keyMatchups.title: Purdy against a depleted back end
keyMatchups.body: San Francisco's passing efficiency leads the league, and Washington ranks 25th defending the pass, now without its every-down safety and two backups. Expect the 49ers to attack the middle of the field and tight ends, where Washington has been worst in the league.

keyMatchups.title: Washington's ground game into a wall
keyMatchups.body: Washington leans run (-3.2 pass rate over expected), and the 49ers allow -0.206 EPA per rush with the fewest explosive runs. If early downs stall, Daniels faces obvious passing situations without Diggs.

keyMatchups.title: No pass rush against a clean pocket
keyMatchups.body: Washington turns pressure into sacks at the 27th-best rate. San Francisco has allowed only three sacks all season. Without a takeaway or a drive-killing sack, Washington has little way to get the 49ers off the field.

nextGame.watch: Whether Bosa plays. Without him, Daniels can hold the ball against a short-handed 49ers front. With him, last week's five sacks could repeat.

restOfSeason.body:
After San Francisco, the schedule softens in the middle: Philadelphia (29th offense) at home, then Arizona (29th defense), Tennessee (0-5, 31st offense) and Houston. That stretch is where the season will be decided. Late trips to Minnesota and Jacksonville, both top-three defenses, are likely losses. The run defense and Daniels' baseline are sustainable. The turnover margin is not, and if it drifts toward even, the close games that Washington has split will tilt the other way, because the pass defense and special teams keep the margin for error thin.

Expect something like a 6-win team: competitive in most Daniels starts, able to beat the bottom of the schedule, and unable to keep good passing offenses out of the end zone. A healthier secondary is the biggest internal lever. A Daniels absence would sink the outlook quickly, given Washington scored 13 points in Mariota's only start.

bets.reason: The net EPA gap is enormous (1st vs 25th), and San Francisco's top-ranked passing game faces a secondary missing three safeties and its starting corner. The 49ers' +2.03 wins over expected and their own defensive absences keep this from being a bigger edge.

San Francisco averages 30.8 points, and Washington allows 29.8 with the league's worst red-zone touchdown rate. A clean-pocket passing attack against a depleted, sack-poor defense is the clearest mismatch on the board.

Four of Washington's five games went over, averaging 52.8 combined points, and San Francisco is missing defensive starters too. Washington's 31-minute time of possession and the 49ers' stout run defense are the brakes, so this is only a modest edge.

confidence.note: Five-game sample with heavy injury churn in the secondary and a quarterback split
